# openobserve_pipeline (Resource)

Manages an OpenObserve pipeline.

A pipeline is a graph. Records enter from a source stream, flow along `edge`s through `node`s that transform or filter them, and land in an output: another stream, or an external endpoint through a pipeline destination.

Reference `openobserve_function.<name>.name` from a function node and `openobserve_pipeline_destination.<name>.name` from a remote_stream node. Those references are what tell Terraform to create the function and destination first, and to destroy the pipeline before them: the server refuses to delete either while a pipeline still uses it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openobserve_stream" "app_logs" {
  name        = "app_logs"
  stream_type = "logs"
}

resource "openobserve_stream" "app_logs_clean" {
  name        = "app_logs_clean"
  stream_type = "logs"
}

resource "openobserve_function" "redact_email" {
  name = "redact_email"

  function = <<-VRL
    .email = "[redacted]"
  VRL
}

# A pipeline is a graph: records enter from the source stream, flow along edges
# through nodes that transform them, and land in an output.
#
# Note that `function_name` references the function resource rather than naming
# it as a string. That reference is what tells Terraform to create the function
# before the pipeline, and to destroy the pipeline before the function. The
# server refuses to delete a function a pipeline still uses, so a literal string
# here would produce a destroy that fails.
resource "openobserve_pipeline" "redact" {
  name        = "redact_pii"
  description = "Strip email addresses before they land"
  stream_name = openobserve_stream.app_logs.name

  node {
    id          = "in"
    type        = "stream"
    stream_name = openobserve_stream.app_logs.name
  }

  node {
    id            = "redact"
    type          = "function"
    function_name = openobserve_function.redact_email.name
  }

  node {
    id          = "out"
    type        = "stream"
    stream_name = openobserve_stream.app_logs_clean.name
  }

  # Edges are multi-line blocks. HCL allows only one argument on a single line,
  # so `edge { from = "a", to = "b" }` is a syntax error.
  edge {
    from = "in"
    to   = "redact"
  }

  edge {
    from = "redact"
    to   = "out"
  }
}

# Forwarding to somewhere outside OpenObserve uses a remote_stream node and a
# pipeline destination. A stream can source only one realtime pipeline, so this
# one reads from its own stream.
resource "openobserve_stream" "audit" {
  name        = "audit_events"
  stream_type = "logs"
}

resource "openobserve_pipeline_destination" "warehouse" {
  name = "warehouse"
  url  = "https://example.com/ingest"
}

resource "openobserve_pipeline" "ship_audit" {
  name        = "ship_audit"
  stream_name = openobserve_stream.audit.name

  node {
    id          = "in"
    type        = "stream"
    stream_name = openobserve_stream.audit.name
  }

  node {
    id               = "out"
    type             = "remote_stream"
    destination_name = openobserve_pipeline_destination.warehouse.name
  }

  edge {
    from = "in"
    to   = "out"
  }
}

# A condition node drops records that do not match, so only what matters flows
# on. `conditions` is a JSON document, so build it with jsonencode().
resource "openobserve_stream" "raw" {
  name        = "raw_events"
  stream_type = "logs"
}

resource "openobserve_pipeline" "errors_only" {
  name        = "errors_only"
  stream_name = openobserve_stream.raw.name

  node {
    id          = "in"
    type        = "stream"
    stream_name = openobserve_stream.raw.name
  }

  node {
    id   = "filter"
    type = "condition"
    # A tree of conditions: `and`, `or` and `not` nest, and the leaves are
    # column/operator/value comparisons. This is the same shape an alert's
    # `custom` conditions take.
    conditions = jsonencode({
      and = [
        { column = "level", operator = "=", value = "error", ignore_case = false },
      ]
    })
  }

  node {
    id          = "out"
    type        = "stream"
    stream_name = openobserve_stream.app_logs_clean.name
  }

  edge {
    from = "in"
    to   = "filter"
  }

  edge {
    from = "filter"
    to   = "out"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Pipeline name. The server trims it and lowercases it, so `My Pipeline` is stored as `my pipeline`. Writing it lowercase avoids the surprise.
- `stream_name` (String) Source stream the pipeline consumes.

A stream can be the source of only one realtime pipeline. A second one is rejected with *A realtime pipeline with same source stream already exists*.

### Optional

- `description` (String) What the pipeline does.
- `edge` (Block List) A directed connection between two nodes. Records flow from `from` to `to`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--edge))
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the pipeline processes records. A disabled pipeline stays configured but idle.
- `node` (Block List) One node of the graph. At least two nodes are required, and every node needs to be reachable from the input node through `edge` blocks. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--node))
- `org_id` (String) Organization the pipeline belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `org_id`.
- `source_type` (String) How the pipeline is triggered. Only `realtime` is supported by this provider today: records are processed as they are ingested into `stream_name`.
- `stream_type` (String) Type of the source stream.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource ID in the format `{org_id}/{pipeline_id}`.
- `pipeline_id` (String) Server-assigned pipeline identifier.
- `version` (Number) Server-maintained revision, bumped on each edit.

<a id="nestedblock--edge"></a>
### Nested Schema for `edge`

Required:

- `from` (String) Source node id.
- `to` (String) Target node id.


<a id="nestedblock--node"></a>
### Nested Schema for `node`

Required:

- `id` (String) Node identifier, unique within the pipeline. `edge` blocks join nodes by this.
- `type` (String) What the node does:

- `stream`: reads from or writes to a stream. Needs `stream_name`.
- `function`: applies a transform. Needs `function_name`.
- `condition`: filters records. Needs `conditions`.
- `remote_stream`: forwards to a pipeline destination. Needs `destination_name`.

Optional:

- `after_flatten` (Boolean) For a `function` node, whether the transform runs after the record is flattened. Defaults to true, and is meaningless on any other node type.
- `conditions` (String) For a `condition` node, the filter as a JSON document. Build it with `jsonencode()`. An empty condition set is rejected by the server.
- `destination_name` (String) For a `remote_stream` node, the destination to forward to. Reference `openobserve_pipeline_destination.<name>.name` so Terraform orders them.
- `function_name` (String) For a `function` node, the transform to apply. Reference `openobserve_function.<name>.name` so Terraform creates it first.
- `io_type` (String) The node's role: `input` for the source, `output` for a terminal node, `default` for anything in between. Inferred when omitted, from the node's type and whether any edge leaves it.
- `position_x` (Number) Horizontal position in the visual editor. Purely cosmetic, and laid out left to right in declaration order when omitted.
- `position_y` (Number) Vertical position in the visual editor. Cosmetic; defaults to 0.
- `stream_name` (String) For a `stream` node, the stream read from or written to.
- `stream_type` (String) For a `stream` node, the type of that stream. Defaults to the pipeline's `stream_type`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Pipelines are imported as {org_id}/{pipeline_id}. The identifier is
# server-assigned, so find it with the openobserve_pipelines data source:
#
#   output "pipeline_ids" {
#     value = { for p in data.openobserve_pipelines.all.pipelines : p.name => p.pipeline_id }
#   }
terraform import openobserve_pipeline.redact default/7497861055431835648
```
